findings.title: Make usage-ledger rotation and recovery atomic with budget summaries
findings.scenario: A summary scans usage.jsonl, releases its lock, then reads usage.rollup. A concurrent rotation folds the scanned receipt into the rollup between those operations, so one receipt is counted twice. Conversely, after a crash between archive rename and rollup write, session_summary/summary return zero for the archived receipt until a writer calls recover_unrolled. Startup and Run::prepare reconcile these incorrect totals into admission state; monotonic reconciliation can retain an inflated charge, and an older snapshot may omit crash-window charges before new paid work.
evidence: Injected current-source cargo test review_probe_summary_racing_rotation_does_not_double_count failed: actual 2, expected 1.
Injected current-source cargo test review_probe_summary_after_rotation_crash_keeps_archived_usage failed: actual 0, expected 1.
Both probes use actual Ledger methods/private-storage helpers; race uses existing with_summary_gate and calls actual rotate while the reader is paused after unlock.
Source restored byte-for-byte after probes. Independent sol reviewer confirmed race trace.
acceptance: Use a stable cross-process coordination primitive spanning active-file generation, archive/rollup publication, recovery and summary snapshot; locking a renamed inode alone is insufficient.
Summary and startup budget reconciliation recover or fail closed on unrolled archives before reporting totals or admitting work.
Deterministic concurrent rotation/summary tests for both full and session checkpoint readers return each receipt exactly once.
Crash injection between rename and rollup write, followed by read-only startup and capped request admission before any flush, preserves charges; concurrent writers cannot lose a rollup generation.

findings.title: Context relief resets interactive and child turn budgets instead of carrying the remainder
findings.failure_scenario: A TUI prompt configured with max_agent_turns=2 runs a tool, crosses the context-relief boundary, then respawns a fresh runner with the same full configured cap. Further tool batches can compact and respawn repeatedly, so neither max_agent_turns nor turn_token_budget bounds the whole prompt. A child with max_turns=2 similarly spends a turn before local context refusal, summarizes, then receives a fresh two-turn exploration allowance; up to two child reliefs multiply the intended exploration budget.
evidence: compact_and_respawn rebuilds/clones the normal agent and calls spawn_runner_paused without any remaining-turn or remaining-token argument (ui/mod.rs 1930-1957).

Each interactive runner initializes max_turns from agent.default_max_turns, turns_used=0, and UsageLedger::default() (runner.rs 4180-4186). No interactive budget-carry state is installed or read; HeadlessBudgetCarry applies only to headless code.

The child relief closure selects ChildRelief::Continue => max_turns on every continuation (task_tool.rs 2183-2185), and run_subagent_with_history constructs a new .max_turns(max_turns) stream (runner.rs 6049-6051). relieve_child_context only sums prior turns after the continuation (task_tool.rs 4276-4286).

CONFIG.md 734/738 promises a cumulative agentic-turn token cap and max model round trips per user prompt; SUBAGENTS.md 1240 promises max agent turns per subagent. djjua repaired precisely this failure in headless without fixing these two seams.
fix_acceptance_tests: Drive the TUI actual mid-turn compact-and-respawn path with a scripted model and max_agent_turns=2; after one completion before relief, permit at most one further completion and retain completed tool effects when the cap stops the prompt.

Exercise interactive turn_token_budget across a successful compaction: cumulative model usage before and after relief must trigger the cap, including the goal/no-session TUI paths newly permitted in this diff.

Exercise the actual child relief closure with max_turns=2 and bulky tool output. The continued exploration must receive only remaining turns across both possible reliefs. Any deliberate tool-free summary/write-up/repair exception must be separately bounded, documented and asserted.

findings.title: TUI byte-pressure relief is silently vetoed by the inner token-only compaction gate
findings.failure_scenario: An image-heavy TUI session exceeds compact_size_fraction of the 32 MiB persistence ceiling but remains well below the model token window. The between-turn detector requests compaction, but handle_compress passes force=false and plan_tui_compaction immediately returns WithinBudget on tokens. Thus the advertised automatic byte relief never runs. During a long tool-heavy prompt the same byte trigger retires and respawns runners on unchanged history at every subsequent tool batch, because a no-op sets no futility floor. Saves can eventually stop at the hard ceiling.
evidence: event_handler.rs 680-691 includes actionable_size_pressure in should_auto_compact_between_turns and then calls handle_compress(None, true, ...).
handle_compress unconditionally forwards force=false (slash/mod.rs 470-478), then handle_compress_with_force passes auto && !force to plan_tui_compaction (514-520).
plan_tui_compaction returns WithinBudget solely when effective_context_tokens_after_tool_result_pruning <= max_tokens (756-760); it has no byte-pressure input.

mid-turn compact_and_respawn passes pressure.is_none() as force (ui/mod.rs 1904-1907). Byte boundaries carry Some(pressure), so this also passes false. The function always spawns another runner after the no-op (1918-1957).

Headless headless_compaction_plan_with explicitly includes actionable_size_pressure (startup.rs 701-710), demonstrating the TUI mismatch. Existing image session tests establish low-token >24MiB pressure but do not traverse this TUI gate.
fix_acceptance_tests: A TUI session above a deliberately small compact_size_fraction, below token pressure, with a legal old prefix must reach a scripted summarizer and install a compaction through the same handler used on Done.

A byte-pressure mid-turn boundary must also reach actual compaction; if retained images make shrinking futile, later batches must remain in the same continuing segment until material growth rearms relief.
Assert no summarizer re-spend/no repeated runner respawn after an unchanged or failed compaction. Keep manual force and token-pressure behavior covered.

findings.title: Repeated tool-call ids restore one file contents under another file path after compaction
findings.failure_scenario: In a headless session, read a.txt with provider call id call-1 succeeds and later read b.txt reuses call-1 but fails with an Error result. findings.title: Split PTY input bypasses the history-expansion guard and executes an unchecked history command
findings.scenario: An interactive bash PTY has an earlier history entry containing a command blocked by the shell deny policy. A history event designator is split across separate job_status input calls. Each chunk passes its individual history guard; the cumulative line is still accepted as read-only text, then bash expands it and executes a command absent from the permission identity.
evidence: history_expansion_trigger(input) is called before pending_input is read, and is not re-run on combined at line 1640 or after prompt baseline changes.
The read-only classifier treats the cumulative event designator as a literal relative operand; the configured shell deny therefore never sees the command bash substitutes.

Existing isolated temp-directory PTY evidence shows the terminal expansion executed the marker-creation command. The output artifact records marker_created: True. No production Cargo/tool invocation was run.
findings.fix: Validate history expansion against the cumulative pending+input inside the epoch/retry loop, after reloading the latest baseline; apply the same validation before a named Enter submits tracked text.
acceptance_tests: Drive a real interactive bash PTY with a seeded history entry containing a denied marker command; split the event designator across input calls. Refuse it before terminal submission and assert the marker remains absent.
Split history expansion designators at every boundary and simulate input arriving during approval; ensure validation is repeated against the latest cumulative baseline.

findings.title: Long-lived provider clients stop refreshing after eight credential rotations
findings.scenario: Construct a provider SDK client with command-issued token S0, keep that client alive, and have the helper issue a different token on each TTL refresh. After tokens S1..S8 are stored, S0 is evicted from known. The SDK continues constructing requests with its baked-in S0.
evidence: store limits known to8 values and removes the oldest token (lines173-176).
apply identifies ownership exclusively by finding the request header/query secret in known (lines224-237), and its rewrite loop also consults known (line265).

On the rotation that evicts S0, the header rewrite skips S0 after refresh; later apply returns None entirely. ProviderHttpClient::send_with_credentials then receives applied.is_empty() and cannot renew/resend on401.

At the default300-second TTL, a helper returning distinct tokens breaks a persistent client after about40minutes; the documented feature explicitly promises old clients continue working without restart.
findings.fix: Associate credential identity with each provider client/request, or retain a stable client credential alias for the full client lifetime; a rolling list of the last eight tokens cannot identify long-lived clients.
acceptance_tests: Build one SDK completion model once, force at least10distinct helper-issued rotations, and assert every request sends the newest token and succeeds.
Cover bearer, x-api-key and Gemini query credentials, including the request causing S0 eviction and a401 renewal after the eighth rotation.

findings.title: Unicode SEARCH text allocates a quadratic fuzzy-mask table before the work budget runs
findings.scenario: Use similarity edit on a one-character file with a single-line SEARCH containing100,000 distinct non-whitespace Unicode scalars (for example U+10000 upward), and any replacement. No exact/normalized match exists. Even with fuzzy:false, find_best_match builds BitParallelPattern before checking candidate bounds.
evidence: find_best_match creates the bit-parallel pattern unconditionally at line424, before skipping unpromising candidates.
BitParallelPattern::new appends ceil(pattern.len()/64) u64 cells for every distinct scalar (lines518-526), with no allocation budget.
For100,000 distinct chars, masks alone require100,000*1,563*8=1,250,400,000bytes, from a400,000-byte SEARCH; temporary capacity growth may require more.

MAX_FUZZY_DISTANCE_WORK is enforced only in distance_within, after this allocation; the one-character candidate would be rejected without any distance work. The old DP work-budget gate was replaced by this allocation path in3999a3f9.
findings.fix: Budget mask construction with checked multiplication and a byte ceiling, or store character masks sparsely; construct patterns only after finding a viable bounded candidate.
acceptance_tests: A bounded test with many distinct Unicode scalars and content="x" returns NotFound/budget error before allocating a dense mask table; verify checked estimated storage is capped.
A large diverse Unicode near-match fails closed within a fixed memory ceiling while normal ASCII/multilingual fuzzy edits still work.

findings.title: Guarded JS absolute-path overwrites discard the checked preimage digest at publication
findings.scenario: Read an allowed absolute-path file completely, then issue JS write_file. After write_guarded_path reads and authorizes the preimage, an editor or other process changes that file before the blocking atomic publisher runs. The JS write replaces the newer contents although the model never read them.
evidence: write_guarded_path checks overwrite proof and computes base at lines2186-2188.
It calls write_approved_file_cancellable at2196 without passing base. Its Replace arm at1647-1654 calls atomic_write_resolved_checked_cancellable.
That fs wrapper passes expected_content=None into atomic_write_resolved_inner (src/fs.rs1405-1418), so it checks parent/path identity but not equality with the authorized preimage.

The bound JS branch correctly uses replace_relative_atomic_expecting(...,&base) at2130; native edit/write use expecting variants. Absolute paths select the ambient path even when they point inside the bound workspace, so this affects more than external roots.
findings.fix: For guarded replacements, use atomic_write_resolved_expecting_cancellable with the computed base and retain the create-only path for new files.
acceptance_tests: Deterministically pause after the overwrite guard, change the target in place to same-length bytes, resume publication, and assert TargetChanged/no overwrite for an absolute workspace path and an allowed external path.
Verify unchanged preimages still replace successfully and cancellation/new-file behavior remains intact.

findings.title: Retire active MCP runs immediately when stdin reaches EOF
findings.scenario: Start a long silent run without a progressToken, then disconnect/close the MCP client stdin while the server remains alive. The run continues issuing model requests and executing tools until it completes or its default 30-minute timeout.
evidence: EOF only sets input_open=false and continues; the loop exits only when !input_open && tasks.is_empty() (1077).
The cancellation send and tasks.shutdown() that activate GroupKillOnDrop are after the loop, at 1177-1180. They cannot execute while the active run prevents tasks.is_empty().
A silent run without progressToken writes no output while working, so even closing client stdout does not provide a write error that would end serve().
The recent client_loss_kills_the_whole_process_group_of_a_running_call test triggers an oversized protocol line, not EOF (1435-1439), leaving this ordinary transport-close branch unproved.
findings.fix: Treat EOF/reader closure as transport retirement, exit the dispatch loop and cancel/join owned runs immediately; retain response draining only for completed work.
acceptance_tests: Use the existing long-child/grandchild fixture, wait for its pid marker, drop client_in without an oversize line and without a progress token, and assert serve returns and both pids terminate within a short deadline. Also close the client output half and prove the same behavior.
findings.final_root_verification: Accepted after independent exact-source control/data-flow review at 83cee733.

findings.title: Guard the headersHelper process group when connection cancellation drops its future
findings.scenario: An opted-in headersHelper starts a child (for example a credential helper shell runs sleep or a cloud login subprocess), then the MCP connection/reconnect is cancelled before the helper finishes. The direct helper is killed but its descendants keep running.
evidence: run() creates a separate Unix process group and retains only a plain tokio Child with kill_on_drop(true), at 112-118.
The whole-group kill is ordinary code after timeout(...).await at 135-138, so dropping run() while it awaits skips it.
client.rs:911-921 explicitly races merged_headers against current_work_scope_cancelled; choosing cancellation drops merged_headers/run(). ServerLink also drops its connector on cancellation.
Existing headersHelper tests cover normal completion, output/exit errors and its own timeout, but no abort/drop cancellation with a descendant.
findings.fix: Use a drop-safe owned process-tree guard for the helper, retaining group ownership through kill/reap on every return, cancellation and future drop.
acceptance_tests: Run a helper that starts a grandchild and records both pids, cancel/drop merged_headers after the marker exists, and assert both processes terminate promptly. Exercise cancellation via connect_bound_with_timeout_in, not only the internal helper timeout.
findings.final_root_verification: Accepted after independent exact-source control/data-flow review at 83cee733.

findings.title: Carry an editor precondition into the write RPC before replacing the live buffer
findings.scenario: With ACP client file access enabled, edit/write re-reads the editor buffer and sees the expected preimage. The user types before the subsequent fs/write_text_file request is applied. The request replaces the entire current document with text computed from the old preimage, silently deleting that user input.
evidence: write_client_text checks current == expected in one read RPC (84-93), then sends a separate write_text(path, content) RPC (94-96) containing no expected content/version.
AcpClientFs::write_text constructs WriteTextFileRequest with only session id, path and replacement content, src/extras/acp/client_fs.rs:141-158.
VS Code writeText opens the now-current document and unconditionally replaces its full range (editors/vscode/src/vscodeClientFs.ts:25-28); nothing compares it to the read used by the agent.

Deterministic probe transpiled the actual vscodeClientFs.ts with a vscode mock: readText returned before, the document changed to before plus user text, then writeText(agent replacement) succeeded with finalText=agent replacement and userEditPreserved=false.
The existing FakeClient typed_meanwhile coverage changes the buffer before the final re-read; it does not cover changes after the check and before write publication.

Explicit documented safeguard: docs/agent/CONFIG.md:3347-3349 says edits/overwrites re-read immediately before publishing and refuse on change, followed by “there is no silent clobber of a buffer edited after the read”. client_fs.rs:66-68 repeats that a buffer edited in the meantime is never overwritten with a stale computation. The split-RPC check cannot fulfill this contract.
findings.fix: Implement an editor-side conditional write/version contract (negotiated ACP extension metadata is one option), so the same operation that applies the edit checks the expected preimage/version. Refuse the editor write when that guarantee is unavailable instead of claiming that an intervening buffer edit can never be overwritten.
acceptance_tests: A cross-RPC fixture must pause after the pre-write read response, edit the document, then deliver the write request; assert a conflict response, preserved user text and no save. Cover changes while the write request awaits realpath/openTextDocument, plus unchanged-buffer success.
findings.final_root_verification: Accepted after independent exact-source control/data-flow review at 83cee733.

findings.title: Map absent workspace destinations when previewing LSP file creation and rename
findings.scenario: A language server returns a valid code action containing CreateFile(/workspace/new.rs) and its initial text edits, or RenameFile(existing.rs,new.rs). Because new.rs does not exist yet, the preview drops the operation and replacement text as outside the workspace.
evidence: navigate() supplies client.parent_path as the URI mapper at navigate.rs:257.
parent_path delegates to parent_diagnostic_uri; that function requires std::fs::canonicalize(target) to succeed at client.rs:1880.

edit_preview applies that mapper to CreateFile.uri, RenameFile.newUri and TextDocumentEdit.textDocument.uri (navigate.rs:480-483,548-559,573-579). Absent in-workspace destinations therefore map to None and increment outside.

The rendered result can say the server returned no edits, with an outside-workspace omission, even though every intended path is inside the retained workspace. Initialization explicitly advertises create/rename resourceOperations.
findings.fix: Give workspace-edit previews a containment mapper that safely handles absent destination components using their retained existing ancestor. Preserve strict existing-file mapping for diagnostics and navigation results.
acceptance_tests: Drive a fake server through the real LspClient URI mapper with a nonexistent in-workspace CreateFile plus TextDocumentEdit, and a RenameFile whose destination is absent. Assert complete intended file operation/replacement previews and outside=0. Keep symlink/traversal/external destinations refused.
findings.final_root_verification: Accepted after independent exact-source control/data-flow review at 83cee733.

findings.title: Escape aliases that already use the ACP reserved alias prefix
findings.scenario: Configure two permitted quick-model names, default and alias:default, pointing to distinct models/providers. ACP advertises both with identical value alias:default. Selecting the default entry instead routes to the literal alias:default model, because parse_model checks exact quick-model keys first.
evidence: wire_value escapes only the literal default alias and leaves alias:default unchanged, producing a duplicate wire value.
parse_model returns the literal configured key at 129-131 before decoding the reserved prefix at 133-137.
Quick-model names are HashMap<String,QuickModelConfig> keys; quoted TOML keys permit colons, and no quick-model alias validation reserves alias:default.
The recent quick_model_named_default_is_selectable_under_a_distinct_value test uses default and fast only, so it does not prove the new wire mapping is injective.
findings.fix: Use an injective encoding for all model aliases (including reserved-prefix aliases), with a separately encoded clear-override sentinel, and decode before lookup consistently.
acceptance_tests: Configure default, alias:default, alias:alias:default and fast simultaneously; assert unique advertised values and that each selection round-trips to precisely its configured alias/provider.
findings.final_root_verification: Accepted after independent exact-source control/data-flow review at 83cee733.
